The leaf is value-named (imported.shared.color-0064e0) so no path channel rule can fire — but all THREE of its axis-expanded refs are `background-color`, on the slider's filled track (part-1-0-1) and its two thumb renderings (slider-thumb, slider-thumb-2). One uniform fill role. Role-grade evidence (c): exactly one candidate is in that role class — {color-border-blue} is a border role, {color-icon-accent} and {color-icon-blue} are icon roles, {color-text-accent} is a text role, and all four are contradicted by three background-color refs. {color-accent} is the accent FILL token and is what Button `primary` already binds for the same surface role. DOCS-THEME.md names this leaf "the single highest-leverage one" in the queue.

literals.reason: ONE LEAF, TWO INCOMPATIBLE ROLES. This value-named shared leaf serves 3 axis-expanded refs that are not the same kind of thing: 1 is a SURFACE (slider tooltip background-color) and 2 are TEXT (slider label-3 color + row-rule-color). The surface role wants {color-background-inverted} (#0A1317 light / #FFFFFF dark) and the text role wants {color-text-primary} or {color-text-gray} (#0A1317 light / #DFE2E5 | #E7EAED dark) — these INVERT against each other in the dark plane, so no single alias can serve both and any choice would silently break one of the two. Fixing it requires SPLITTING the leaf into a surface leaf and a text leaf, which is a path change, which this round forbids. Kept literal with a named follow-up rather than half-fixed.

_literalsMarker: THE OTHER HALF OF A REVIEW. `literals` rows write NOTHING to the minted tree — they receipt a leaf that was looked at and DELIBERATELY kept literal, so "reviewed and refused" stops being indistinguishable from "nobody looked yet". They are validated like aliases (right ack, leaf exists, leaf is not already aliased, value re-checked against the live tree) and they move the leaf out of the pending queue in `reanchor-proposals.md`. TO RE-OPEN a leaf: delete its row here and re-run --propose.
